title: SRE Rapid Response: API Signals & Playnotes
body:
Purpose
This is a working draft of quick-response guidance for common API degradations we see in Redwood’s hosted endpoints: request timeouts, 429 rate limiting spikes, degraded streaming (partial frames/early EOF), and sudden elevation in 5xx/4xx error rates. The intent is to give an on-call responder a concise prioritized checklist, common diagnostic commands, and tactical mitigations that are low-risk and fast.

Tone: pragmatic, scratchpad-style. Keep things short for pager-context. 

TL;DR quick checklist (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm scope: which route(s), region(s), customer tiers are affected (console + incidents dashboard).
- Check traffic and errors: traffic delta, 5xx/4xx/timeout rate, p50/p95 latency, streaming disconnects.
- If error rate > threshold or latency p95 > SLO: initiate mitigation lane (scale, throttle, fallback).
- Notify stakeholders: ping infra-oncall, product-owner, CS for customer-facing incidents if customer impact visible.

Detection signals and where to look (one-liners)
- Synthetic monitors: failed probes show 5xx or non-200 body. Console -> Monitors -> Most recent run.
- Edge gateway logs: surge of upstream_429 / upstream_timeout entries.
- Runtime metrics: kv-cache miss spikes, queue depth, batching latency increase. Serving runtime dashboard -> per-model route.
- Network errors: TCP retransmits, TLS handshake timeouts in host-level monitoring. Infra monitoring -> host network.
- Logs: look for repeating error strings (Context: rateLimiter.allow failed / kvcache lookup timed out / stream eof early).

First triage (0–15m) - rapid scope and cause hypothesis
1) Scope by route and region: filter traces by route and region in tracing UI. If single-customer path, tag incident P1 and notify account-specific CS & AE.
2) Is it capacity-related? Check dedicated GPU pool metrics, pod/gpu util, queue length, and autoscaler events.
   - If GPU util ~100% and queue length growing => capacity saturation hypothesis.
3) Is it a throttling/429 origin? Correlate ingress rate to upstream 429 logs and token bucket metrics.
4) Is it degraded streaming? Check stream connection lifetimes, per-connection error frames, and whether client-side cancels are inflating disconnects.
5) Are deployments/rollouts in last 30–60 minutes? Look at rollout events in Console and recent PRs/CI.

Basic diagnostic commands and quick queries
- k8s: kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide | grep <route-model>
- logs: kubectl -n serving logs -l route=<route> --since=15m | egrep "(timeout|rateLimiter|kvcache|eof|connection reset)"
- promql samples: rate(api_request_errors_total[1m]) by (route), histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- gRPC/stream checks: tail stream logs for frame-level errors and look for repeated CANCELLED/UNAVAILABLE codes.

Common root causes & fast mitigations (map cause -> immediate action)
- Cause: Autoscaler lag / insufficient pool capacity
  Action: Temporarily increase pool size / unpin more instances to route (if Dedicated) OR promote fallback model variant with lower cost-per-token. Add temporary burst nodes if available.
- Cause: Thundering client retry storms -> load spike -> 429s + queueing
  Action: Apply global ingress smoothing: enable conservative rate-limit at edge, add short (10–30s) global backoff headers to clients via gateway, and trigger graceful degrade path (reduce max tokens / shorter context).
- Cause: Runtime kernel issue / memory leak => elevated latency/5xx
  Action: Roll back recent serving runtime deploy if rollout present; switch traffic to previous stable variant. Engage infra-engineering.
- Cause: External dependency timeout (e.g., KMS, feature store, metadata service) causing request-level timeouts
  Action: Flip circuit breaker for that dependency path, re-route requests to cached path, or return synthetic fallback outputs (best-effort) while dependency recovered.
- Cause: Stream-level fragmentation from client-side timeouts
  Action: Extend streaming keepalive and increase read timeout on gateway (small increment), advise SDK teams to backoff client retransmits.

Low-risk tactical mitigations (good for P1s with customer impact)
- Traffic routing: Promote a lower-latency model variant for the affected route and weight-swap traffic (canary -> 100%). This reduces per-request processing and may reduce queue length.
- Soft throttle: At the ingress layer apply a short-lived quota for noisy clients (observed by client_id or IP) and return Retry-After headers.
- Shorten max_tokens (server-side override) for high-latency routes to reduce token-cost and inference time.
- Enable prefix/KV cache warmups for hot prefixes (manual warmup if cache cold).

Escalation ladder (when to call who)
- If mitigation in 10m doesn't reduce error rate by 50%: page serving-runtime engineering + infra oncall.
- If rollback needed or kernel-level debugging: page runtime-ownership lead (Marco Liu).
- If customer SLA breach imminent or multiple enterprise customers affected: page account-ops + CS director (Rina Shah).

Responder playbook: step-by-step
1) (0–5m) Confirm alerts and set incident channel (inc-<shortid>). Record affected routes and customers.
2) (5–15m) Run triage queries above, capture p95/p99 and error rates. Try first low-risk mitigations: ingress throttle, promote fallback model, shorten max_tokens.
3) (15–40m) If no improvement: start scaling actions (add capacity/pools), and prepare a rollback of recent deploys. Take targeted traffic off the problematic cluster if available.
4) (40–90m) If root cause is unclear: gather heap/profile dumps (if safe), preserve logs, and escalate to runtime and infra. Keep stakeholders informed every 30m.
5) (post-stabilization) Capture timeline, customer impact, and open follow-ups.

Communication templates (short)
- Initial note (channel/inc-1234): "We are investigating elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects on route /v1/generate in us-west1. Hypothesis: serving pool saturation. Mitigations in flight: ingress smoothing + promoting lower-cost model variant. Will update in 15m."
- Customer-facing (CS): "We are actively mitigating an availability issue affecting model responses in US-West. Expected resolution: 30–60 minutes. We will apply traffic smoothing and an internal fallback; no data loss is expected."

Post-incident capture (must-haves)
- What changed in last 72h (deployments, infra changes, config flips).
- Metrics at start/peak/stable: p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, traffic.
- Mitigations attempted and the exact steps/command used.
- Root cause (confirmed or probable) and why.
- Affected customers and SLA impact.
- Action items and owners (assign in Jira).

Open experiments and ideas (scratchpad)
- Client-visible Retry-After header experiments: dynamic vs static values; measure retry storms.
- Adaptive max_tokens per customer type based on real-time queue depth.
- Lightweight prefork warm pools for hot prefixes to reduce cold-start jitter.
- Better synthetic stream-level probes (frame-level validation) to detect early EOF patterns faster.

Notes to oncall (practical tips)
- When in doubt, reduce surface area: prefer routing traffic away from suspect cluster over incremental risky kernel changes.
- Small changes + quick observation cycles beat big undiagnosed flips.
- Keep a record of exact kubectl/console actions (we often need to reproduce during postmortem).

Known short-term TODOs in this doc
- Add exact PromQL queries for our new metrics names (update when new telemetry lands). OWNER: Ethan. DUE: 2025-02-10.
- Create a small script to promote fallback model variants safely via Console API. OWNER: Marco. DUE: 2025-02-17.

Random operator heuristics (from recent oncall)
- If you see a rapid p95 jump with flat traffic: look for kernel-level GC or io-saturation first.
- 429 spikes + downstream 502s often mean a burst of aggressive client retries collapsing a dependency—throttle clients ASAP.
- For streaming issues: examine client SDK release notes; older SDKs occasionally retry incorrectly and cause connection churn.

Appendix: quick links
- Serving runtime dashboards: Console -> Observability -> Serving runtime
- Incident tracker template: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SRE/Incident+Template
- Rollout dashboard: Console -> Deployments -> Recent rollouts

End of draft.

(Sign-off) Working draft — feedback welcome. This doc is intentionally terse to optimize read time during noisy incidents.
